public import FormalConjecturesUtil
public import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«507»

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 77

*Reference:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 77](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.77)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Erdos507 Filter Topology

namespace Green77

/--
Given $n$ points in the unit disc, must there be a triangle of area at most $n^{-2+o(1)}$
determined by them?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem green_77 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ), Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
      α ≪ fun n ↦ n ^ (-2 + o n) := by
  sorry

end Green77

reformulations.difference: Instead of explicitly quantifying over point configurations and triangles, Lean bounds the supremum Erdos507.α using Big-O and an exponent correction tending to zero. The supremum excludes wholly collinear configurations.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each finite configuration with at least three points, the unsigned triangle areas form a finite nonempty set, so their infimum is attained. These minima are uniformly bounded on the unit disc, making the supremum an ordinary bounded real supremum. Excluded collinear configurations already contain zero-area triples. Consequently, bounding α is equivalent to the uniform triangle-existence assertion. A positive Big-O constant C is absorbed by replacing o(n) with o(n) + log(C)/log(n), which still tends to zero. The converse uses Big-O constant 1. The complete equivalence with a direct eventual triangle-existence statement was proved as review_equivalence in the scratch file; its axioms exclude sorryAx.

sources_consulted: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.77 — Problem 77, p. 37, including its comments and 2023/2025 updates; also the introductory notation conventions.
https://arxiv.org/e-print/2305.18253 — Cohen, Pohoata and Zakharov, A new upper bound for the Heilbronn triangle problem, LaTeX source, §§1–2.
review.notes: Checked the sole theorem and its imported geometric and asymptotic definitions. Lean experiments verified α(0)=α(1)=α(2)=0, nonnegativity, boundedness of the supremum's defining set, attainment of the triangle-area minimum for configurations of size at least three, and area 1/2 for the standard right triangle. The small-cardinality defaults do not affect the asymptotic assertion. Green's source still records the problem as open. erdosproblems.com/507 was Cloudflare-blocked despite a descriptive User-Agent; the directly cited Green source and the primary paper were accessible and sufficient. All Lean experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.
